stories.headline: Bipartisan Lawmakers Say It’s Time to Rethink America’s Fragile Childcare System
facts: Title: Bipartisan Lawmakers Say It’s Time to Rethink America’s Fragile Childcare System
_Join our zero2eight Substack community for more discussion about the latest news in early care and education._[**Sign up today.**](https://zero2eight.substack.com/)
CHICAGO — A bipartisan group of state lawmakers is calling for an overhaul of the nation’s childcare system, which they say is failing children, parents and providers.

The group of 13 Republican and Democratic lawmakers, who have spent the last year studying childcare access and affordability problems, offered an array of policy recommendations during the National Conference of State Legislatures annual summit in Chicago this week.

During a panel discussion Monday, lawmakers underscored the persisting challenge with childcare that costs families too much and pays providers too little. That has led to vast access gaps in many parts of the country as demand for childcare far outstrips supply.

A major and final piece of West Virginia lawmakers’ 2023 hallmark education legislation goes into effect this school year when schools are required to retain third graders whose reading and math abilities aren’t at grade level.
